# Training Optimization and Initialization
## Overview
This family covers the initialization strategies and iterative optimization procedures required to reconstruct 3D scenes from 2D images using 3D Gaussian Splatting [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It solves the problem of converting sparse or dense image collections into a set of differentiable volumetric primitives that can be rendered in real time [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. It differs from implicit neural field methods by optimizing explicit, static or dynamic ellipsoids via differentiable rasterization, achieving faster convergence and rendering speeds [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
## Shared principles
All methods in this family optimize a set of $N$ 3D Gaussian primitives [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Each primitive $i$ is defined by position $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ [G], rotation $q_i \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (unit quaternion) [G], scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ [G], opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$ [G], and appearance parameters such as spherical harmonic coefficients $h_i$ [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The optimization minimizes a loss function $\mathcal{L}$ between rendered images and ground truth views, typically using the Adam optimizer [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The rendering process involves projecting 3D Gaussians to 2D screen space, sorting by depth, and alpha blending [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md].
## Subtopics

### [3DGS Initialization Policy](1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md)
A deterministic strategy for placing $N$ Gaussians within a bounding volume. It sets apart from heuristic methods by using a fixed power-law scaling for initial opacity to ensure consistent integrated opacity regardless of $N$ [1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md]. Choose this for reproducible baselines in synthetic scenes.

### [3D Gaussian Splatting Training](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md)
The core iterative optimization loop for static scenes. It initializes Gaussians from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) points and uses adaptive density control (splitting/cloning/pruning) to refine geometry [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. Choose this for high-fidelity reconstruction of static scenes from image collections.

### [GauFRe](7994-gaufre.md)
A method for dynamic scenes that decouples static and dynamic components. It initializes points into static and dynamic subsets and optimizes them independently, using compact MLPs for deformation [7994-gaufre.md]. Choose this when the scene contains significant static background and moving foreground elements.

### Training Optimization
Joint optimization of network weights, feature grids, and latent codes using the total training loss [S1]. Learnable parameters include $\Theta_s$ (SDF model), $\Theta_d$ (DDF model), $M$ (SDF and DDF feature grids, $M = (M_s, M_d)$), $M_s = \{M^s_i \mid i = xy, yz, zx\}$, $M_d = \{M^d_i \mid i = pxpy, \dots, rzrx\}$, and $Z$ (set of latent codes for $J$ training shapes, $Z = \{z_i \mid i = 1 \dots J\}$) [S1]. Loss weights are $w_s, w_d, w_\sigma, w_{tv}, w_{ts}, w_l$ [S1].

## Background
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md]. The initialization policy using power-law opacity scaling was detailed in [1398-3dgs-initialization-policy.md]. GauFRe was proposed to address optimization instability in dynamic scenes by separating static and dynamic components [7994-gaufre.md].
